requirements.requirement: Install AIDE and initialize a file-integrity database covering /etc on node1
requirements.summary: aide 0.19.2 was installed via dnf (cmd-f4ce1b6f9fcb4815) and aide --init was run successfully producing a 1131-entry database that was activated as /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz (cmd-cf5a00122886471a, cmd-ad48b3ccb1914887; final re-init cmd-d986d997bd4c4c80, cmd-3a49e321cbdd46d8).

requirements.requirement: Baseline actually tracks content changes to /etc files (not merely permissions)
requirements.summary: Executor identified that the default /etc catch-all rule was PERMS-only (cmd-60d2bd805fea456b) and upgraded it to NORMAL, which includes hashing, then re-initialized the database under this config (cmd-41da1847e2d24bf2, cmd-d986d997bd4c4c80).

requirements.requirement: Baseline is clean/functional immediately after establishment (no false positives)
requirements.summary: Multiple aide --check runs against the final config/database report 'NO differences... Looks okay' with a consistent 1131-entry count.

requirements.requirement: Later changes to /etc files can be identified and reported by the baseline (core task outcome)
requirements.summary: A deliberate content edit to /etc/motd was detected by aide --check, which reported it as a 'Changed' entry with a size and multi-algorithm hash diff, directly demonstrating the reporting capability the task asked for.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered baseline state on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id, db checksum, and clean check were captured (cmd-d38d82965b234ca7); a detached reboot returned an acknowledgement before disconnect (cmd-cdea8601c0254a73); connection failures during the reboot window were followed by a new boot_id (cmd-79cccd0f58854c9d, cmd-ee8329a41db94b22, cmd-2cfa24eb55e8456c, cmd-70043131ced44767), matching the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check (bf4e9cbb... -> 4e4bd6a3...); post-restart the same db checksum, config, and a clean aide --check were reconfirmed (cmd-e3f76a220b6140fc).

overall_summary: The executor established a functioning AIDE-based integrity baseline for /etc on node1, correctly identified and fixed a real gap (the stock PERMS-only catch-all rule would miss content-only edits), and directly proved detection works via a controlled /etc/motd change that was cleanly reverted afterward. The mandatory restart protocol was executed and evidenced end-to-end: pre-restart healthy state, reboot acknowledgement, boot-identity change, and full post-restart recovery of the baseline (matching checksum, config, and clean check), consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence.
limitations: Minor unremoved temporary files (/tmp/aide_init.log, /tmp/aide_init.pid, /tmp/reboot.log) remain on node1 after the task; low-risk but not cleaned up.

No automated recurring check (e.g., cron/systemd timer) for AIDE was found or apparently configured (cmd-774845cf96504552 shows no cron job), though the task only required establishing the baseline itself, not scheduling ongoing checks, so this is not scored as a shortfall.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands mutating state on node1 were: aide install; aide.conf edits (scoping and PERMS->NORMAL upgrade) — all directly required; two rounds of `aide --init` where an earlier attempt (cmd-9ee4b546fd374d66) failed due to a config syntax error introduced by an intermediate sed edit and was corrected by follow-up seds (cmd-dc61bbf314e6416b, cmd-581266bbaf00449d) and a successful re-init (cmd-cf5a00122886471a) — this is a self-corrected configuration mistake, not an unrelated experiment, so it is treated leniently; two bounded test edits to /etc/motd used to prove detection (cmd-0dd7afd8e00347ed, cmd-e48511b58cb444a2) were both fully reverted to the original empty file (cmd-f0bda02e16e747d0, cmd-4cff57759def4022), confirmed by the final post-restart clean check. The main residue is housekeeping: /tmp/aide_init.log, /tmp/aide_init.pid, and /tmp/reboot.log were left on node1 after the task (visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot) instead of being cleaned up; these are low-risk stray files with no functional impact but are unnecessary retained artifacts. /etc/aide.conf.orig was intentionally kept as a backup, which is reasonable and not penalized. The mandatory reboot is an expected state change under the restart protocol.
